C-SELECTED-CLOSE-BOUNDARY-1-7CADD2ED.IntentSummary:
T1 plan for the approved selected-close boundary and query location slice. One cohesive sequential task covers the accepted behavior. The product scope is exactly `src/gates/ledger.ts` and `src/gates/core.test.ts` (`M-GATES`) plus `src/query/change.ts` and `src/query/change.test.ts` (`M-QUERY`); both modules and their `V-M-*` anchors are covered, and the three ordinary criteria (`AC-EVIDENCE-CONSUMABILITY`, `AC-EVALUATION-SNAPSHOT`, `AC-QUERY-PHASE`) are mapped through `Satisfies`. `AC-PHASE-BEFORE-STATUS`, `AC-ARCHIVE-PRESERVATION` and `AC-BOUNDED-WRITES` are close-bound and are implementation obligations of the task, never `Satisfies` targets, and their CloseEvidence commands are not duplicated here. The preservation base stays `156c67c74a10b50478a9752189e47c00544847d2`; the approval checkpoint `12e2e4ffade6105d99efa2dc19398c5ea660d221` is not that base and never replaces it.
The plan implements the approved `AC-EVALUATION-SNAPSHOT` byte guarantee literally. A measured, authority-reproduced current defect: `src/gates/ledger.ts:447-448,467-468` reads spec and ledger as UTF-8 strings, so different byte sequences can decode equally; on a fresh complete adopting project a valid UTF-8 U+FFFD marker (`EF BF BD`) was changed by the real CloseEvidence command to raw `80`, the spec bytes and length changed, the decoded strings stayed equal, and the real pass verdict wrongly appended a ledger. The task must snapshot and recheck spec, plan and ledger as raw buffers (or an equivalent lossless byte comparison) with explicit present-versus-absent handling, decoding for XML validation being a separate operation, while keeping directory identity and location checks and command-side-effect preservation.
No new helper implementation file or export, no shared grammar change or grammar test, no warning-output API, no status/review/catalog change, no graph or verification write, no record or `Pays`, and no README, examples, metadata or stash change. Private expressions or functions inside the already-scoped files are a plan choice.
The sanctioned close performs its ordinary own-bundle lifecycle writes: `ngrace gate verdict` persists the Verdict and its `CloseEvidence` children in the bundle's `run-ledger.xml`; `ngrace apply` writes `applied` status onto the bundle's `spec.xml` and `plan.xml`, writes the applied Decisions and fingerprints into `run-ledger.xml`, and then renames the bundle directory; the cursor, attempt and fold commands own the bundle's `run.xml`, `run/**` and ledger epoch state; the candidate and run-write locks are temporary coordination created and removed by the CLI. These are the CLI's own-bundle effects, excluded by the scope audit's own-bundle identity and CLI-lifecycle rules, so they are deliberately not re-listed in `ObservedWriteScope` or as persistent lock exceptions. Rule 6's project-specific flush and retirement teaching is inapplicable here: this bundle declares no `Pays`, no record conversion and no retirement move.
All local fixture, CLI and lint evidence is POSIX/Bun; no hosted Windows or Dart job is claimed. `TargetAssertions` declares exactly the three close-time leaves `bun run validate:ci`, `bun run validate:cli` and `bun run release:check`; full CI-equivalent verification is close-time only under one outermost `--assertions final --run-commands`, and none of these leaves is driven at PLAN. The approved SPEC overrides `ngrace-plan` rule 19's conflicting full-CI-at-PLAN teaching; that teaching repair belongs to the third authorized slice.

T-001.Title: Bind the selected-close boundary strictly and repair the query phase classifier

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first evidence, captured on a disposable project copy before the corresponding runtime repair and recorded with actual command output and exact restoration, for each separable mechanism: (i) the selected-close consumer accepts a selected archive record with a missing/unparseable spec, wrong root, non-applied status, missing plan, or malformed/duplicate wrapper and appends a ledger; (ii) explicit legacy-`<Criterion>`, nested, or duplicate complete direct `CloseEvidence` is skipped or only partially run while a `pass` is recorded; (iii) a valid UTF-8 U+FFFD marker (`EF BF BD`) in the selected spec is replaced by raw `80` during a `CloseEvidence` command, the decoded strings stay equal, and a real pass verdict still appends; (iv) `collectChangeView` reports `archive` for an active approved bundle under a misleading `changes/archive` parent while a neutral parent reports `active`. Each red is captured before its repair; no later guard is prelanded and no retrospective red is manufactured. A guard cluster that is one indivisible mechanism is driven as a single atomic red/green pair only when its guards necessarily green together; otherwise fail and pass cycles are interleaved and the grouping is disclosed.

Phase before status. In `src/gates/ledger.ts` (`M-GATES`), the selected-close path classifies the explicitly resolved selected bundle relative to this project's `.ngrace/changes/active/` and `.ngrace/changes/archive/` directories before any parsed status can cause an early return. For a selected archive bundle it requires both selected files to exist and parse, the exact registered roots `NgraceChangeSpec` and `NgraceChangePlan`, `status="applied"` on both, and exactly one direct C-* wrapper in each equal to the selected directory/argument identity; it then runs the exported `validateChangeArtifact` on each with the archive location and `projectRoot`, plus `validateSpecPlanCoverage` on this pair. An invalid selected record refuses before any evidence command runs and before any verdict append; required/meaningful sections, AC values, task shapes and selected coverage cannot be bypassed. The strict consumer reads only this selected record: no unrelated bundle enumeration, whole-project validation, historical compatibility reader or schema-version dispatch. Normal active and pre-archive routes retain `CloseEvidence` inertness and are not subjected to archive-only applied requirements. The deliberately lint-invalid active-applied phase control (an active bundle carrying `status="applied"`) is used only to isolate phase routing under neutral and misleading parents and is never presented as a valid record; hand-placed synthetic archive controls are not actual apply/archive lifecycle evidence.

Consumable evidence, not silent absence. In `src/gates/ledger.ts` (`M-GATES`), every explicit `CloseEvidence` declaration in the selected `AcceptanceCriteria` is inspected before evaluation and must be exactly one direct `CloseEvidence` on its bound `AC-*`, with at least one non-empty direct `Command`. Calling the exported `validateChangeArtifact` already refuses a direct empty `CloseEvidence`, a whitespace-only direct `Command`, and a `CloseEvidence` containing only a nested `Command`, each as one error-severity `change.close-evidence-incomplete` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:1899-1907,2203-2205`); the narrow local guard refuses a declaration under a legacy `<Criterion>`, a `CloseEvidence` nested below its `AC-*`, and a duplicate complete direct `CloseEvidence` block, none of which the exported validator detects. Any error-severity issue from the selected spec validation, the selected plan validation, the selected spec-to-plan coverage, or the local evidence-consumption guard refuses the close before any evidence command runs and before any verdict append. Ordinary `AC-*` criteria without evidence and meaningful legacy/free-text criteria without evidence remain legitimate zero-command closes; invalid explicit evidence is never treated as a zero-command close. Warning-severity issues remain advisory: warning-only otherwise-valid artifacts stay admissible, unmapped ordinary criteria, excess plan anchors and undiscriminating command shapes stay advisory, and no warning channel is added to gate output. The current grammar is reused and no whole-project validator or historical reader is invoked.

Preserved evaluation and byte-level snapshot. In `src/gates/ledger.ts` (`M-GATES`), all bound criteria are evaluated; within one criterion evaluation stops at the first non-zero command and continues with the remaining criteria. Each close-bound criterion's evaluation is recorded as a direct `Verdict` child named by its `AC-*` tag, carrying an `Exit` child and a `Result` child, alongside the Verdict's direct `Finding` and `Ack` children (`src/gates/ledger.ts:572-580`, assembled at `:533`). A failed command refuses `outcome pass` without a verdict write; a legitimate `outcome fail` may record the failed-command evaluations. The bound finding/ACK/digest behavior, ledger pre/post-write validation and restoration, candidate lock behavior, and the existing stale-location/directory/spec/ledger checks are preserved. The decision-bearing snapshot and the final equality check compare spec, plan and ledger as raw bytes (or an equivalent lossless byte comparison) with explicit present-versus-absent handling, replacing the current UTF-8 string reads at `src/gates/ledger.ts:447-448,467-468`; decoding for XML validation is a separate operation. A command-induced plan change, and a raw byte change whose decoded text is equal, each refuse append exactly as a spec, ledger, location or identity change does. Refusal preserves the ledger state at the append boundary, including legitimate bytes changed by the probe itself; no rollback of command side effects is claimed. The snapshot covers spec/plan/ledger/directory, not `.ngrace-lint.json`'s advisory command-shape configuration. A regression drives a changed raw byte with equal decoded text, with non-mutating and exact-restoration controls.

Query phase from the resolved project. In `src/query/change.ts` (`M-QUERY`), `collectChangeView` derives the bundle location from the resolved project's bundle path, not from an absolute-path substring in a parent directory; the current absolute-substring test at `src/query/change.ts:84-86` is replaced. Independent controls: an active approved bundle retains active scopes under a neutral and a misleading `changes/archive` parent; a genuine applied archive retains archive scopes under both; retained scopes, criterion and verdict tallies, absent/unparseable artifact distinctions and exact read-only tree equality are preserved. This does not claim that the separate status-dependent surface is archive-free.

Verification feasibility, probe matrix and evidence honesty. The approved `ExpectedEvidence` matrix is proved at Execute with new real-CLI probes on fresh complete synthetic adopting projects that use fresh real owned fixture paths within `src/gates/core.test.ts` and `src/query/change.test.ts`, existing `writeChangeBundleFixture` / minimal-project support, and byte snapshots; no fixture or helper source edit is needed. Spec and plan are tested separately for: missing, unparseable, wrong root, wrong or duplicate direct identity wrapper, missing or non-applied status, malformed required sections or applicable AC/task values, and selected spec-to-plan coverage errors. For each invalid selected archive input, refusal must occur before any evidence command marker runs and must preserve the ledger bytes at the append boundary; each fixture is restored and the admissible control is driven. All explicit-evidence invalid forms, the warning-only control and the legitimate no-evidence control are driven; normal active evidence inertness, the deliberately lint-invalid active-applied routing isolation under neutral and misleading parents, and genuine applied archive controls are driven. Gates and query each have their own route discriminator. A valid multi-criterion, multi-command fixture exercises successful sequencing, first-non-zero short-circuit of later commands within one criterion while a later criterion still executes, refusal of `outcome pass` without append, and a legitimate `outcome fail` that records the evaluations as direct Verdict `AC-*` children carrying `Exit` and `Result` beside the Verdict's `Finding` and `Ack` children. Command-induced spec, plan, ledger, location and directory-identity changes, including present-versus-absent transitions, each refuse append and preserve the ledger bytes at the append boundary, including bytes the command itself changed; no command-side-effect rollback is claimed, and the ACK/digest, pre/post-write validation and restoration, and lock counterweights are preserved. The lossless raw-byte snapshot regression and its non-mutating and exact-restoration controls are retained: spec, plan and ledger are compared as raw bytes with explicit presence states while XML decoding stays a separate operation, and the measured current defect (valid `EF BF BD` becomes raw `80` while both decode alike) must go red and then pass after repair. Where a probe spies on a read it observes through a call-through that records the call and calls the original export, and every zero-read assertion is paired with that route's own positive control; every probe is failure-safe with temp roots and spied modules cleaned up and inputs exactly restored. Existing tests may carry preserved counterweights when they are inspected and demonstrated, and new defect reds are distinguished from controls that were already green; no red-first failure is manufactured. The active applied classifier control is deliberately lint-invalid and isolated to phase routing; synthetic hand-placed archive controls are reader controls, not actual apply/archive evidence. Execute separately rehearses the sanctioned lifecycle on a faithful disposable copy carrying the exact live artifacts and untracked events, fresh default finding ACKs, terminal/fold, apply/archive, selected post-archive verdict/evidence, applied fingerprints and byte preservation. The unchanged narrow command carries its authority baseline by identity. Newly introduced narrow commands and the structural `BaselineAssertions` and `TargetAssertions` are driven on a disposable approved-shaped copy: baseline green, intended target pre-implementation reds recorded honestly, and command-not-evaluated distinguished from command success. No unevaluated command is claimed to have passed. Final CI and CLI validation (`bun run validate:ci`, `bun run validate:cli`, `bun run release:check`) is exempt from PLAN driving and runs only at Execute final; the root current-mode lint is pre-write only and is never a task or target command.
